claude.country: International (ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and EUCLID multinational trials)
claude.sample_unit: suspected EUCLID primary end point events

links.outcome: Hybrid adjudication with human review of lowest-certainty AI predictions versus AI alone, F1 and correct classification
links.effect: Hybrid correctly classified 95.6% of end points vs 86.4% ADAPT-CEC and 76.3% GPT-4o; hybrid F1 highest (CV death 0.94, MI 0.80, stroke 0.82, bleeding 0.83).
links.quote: A hybrid approach with humans adjudicating those suspected events with the lowest 30% of ADAPT-CEC prediction certainty was superior to ADAPT-CEC alone or GPT 4o alone and replicated the EUCLID primary outcome treatment effect.

links.outcome: Performance of trial-derived AI on a second trial and new end points after brief adaptation
links.effect: After adaptation with 20 EUCLID events per end point, ADAPT-CEC adjudicated MI, stroke, CV death and bleeding and replicated primary treatment effect (HR 0.98 vs human 1.02).
links.quote: After brief adaptation, a single trial-derived AI algorithm can adjudicate similar (MI and stroke) and new end points (CV death and bleeding) in a second trial and replicate the EUCLID primary outcome treatment effect.

links.outcome: Adaptation of model using small sample of new-trial events for external validation performance
links.effect: Adapting with 20 EUCLID suspected events per end point allowed ADAPT-CEC to classify 86.4% of end points correctly and replicate the EUCLID primary treatment effect (HR 0.98).
links.quote: ADAPT-CEC was derived from myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and heart failure from the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES (Evaluation of Cardiovascular Outcomes After an Acute Coronary Syndrome During Treatment With Alirocumab) trial and externally validated on MI, stroke, bleeding and cardiovascular (CV) death from the EUCLID (Examining Use of Ticagrelor in Peripheral Artery Disease) trial after adaptation with 20 EUCLID suspected events per end point.

links.outcome: Comparison of AI strategies against human adjudication and each other on the same data
links.effect: ADAPT-CEC, hybrid, and GPT-4o correctly classified 86.4%, 95.6%, and 76.3% of end points versus human adjudication; ADAPT-CEC bleeding F1 0.78 superior to GPT-4o.
links.quote: ADAPT-CEC was compared via F1 score with direct Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) 4o adjudication and a hybrid approach where the 30% of suspected events with the lowest AI prediction certainty used human adjudication.

unlisted_practices: Using AI prediction certainty to triage lowest-certainty cases to human adjudication in clinical trial end point adjudication

openai.sample_unit: suspected EUCLID primary end point events

links.effect: Hybrid F1 metrics were highest; ADAPT-CEC was lower for CV death, MI, and stroke, while bleeding F1 0.78 was superior to GPT 4o.
links.quote: ADAPT-CEC F1 metrics were lower for CV death, MI, and stroke but similar to GPT 4o, while bleeding (0.78 [95% CI, 0.77-0.79]) was superior to GPT 4o.

links.outcome: F1 scores after routing low-certainty cases to humans
links.effect: Hybrid adjudication had highest F1: CV death 0.94, MI 0.80, stroke 0.82, bleeding 0.83.
links.quote: Hybrid adjudication F1 metrics were the highest (CV death, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.92-0.96]; MI, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.77-0.82]; stroke, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.78-0.86]; bleeding, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.82-0.85]).

links.effect: ADAPT-CEC, hybrid, and GPT 4o correctly classified 86.4%, 95.6%, and 76.3% of endpoints; non-endpoints 99.4%, 99.6%, and 99.8%.
links.quote: Among 13 885 suspected EUCLID primary end point events, ADAPT-CEC, hybrid, and GPT 4o strategies correctly classified 86.4%, 95.6%, and 76.3% of all end points and 99.4%, 99.6%, and 99.8% of all non-end points compared with human adjudication, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Brief adaptation of an event-adjudication AI with 20 suspected events per endpoint for new endpoint definitions

links.effect: Hybrid adjudication correctly classified 95.6% of endpoints compared with 86.4% for ADAPT-CEC alone and 76.3% for GPT-4o, and achieved the highest F1 metrics across all endpoints.
links.quote: Among 13 885 suspected EUCLID primary end point events, ADAPT-CEC, hybrid, and GPT 4o strategies correctly classified 86.4%, 95.6%, and 76.3% of all end points and 99.4%, 99.6%, and 99.8% of all non-end points compared with human adjudication, respectively.

screen.reason: The study tests a deployment/operational strategy of hybrid human-in-the-loop adjudication, selectively routing the 30% of cases with the lowest AI prediction certainty to human adjudicators, and compares it against purely automated AI strategies.
